title: Final settlement of unabsorbable losses cuts the USDS target price and compensates holders with 24 billion SKY
content:
A.3.7.1.6.2 completes the loss waterfall. After the Genesis Capital haircut, if losses still exceed the Prime Agent's capital plus Aggregate Backstop Capital, the SKY Backstop activates and "the SKY mint must be sized to cover the remaining loss." And if losses exceed even that: "Sky will adjust the USDS target price below $1 to the extent necessary to settle the remaining deficit; Sky will then distribute 24 billion SKY to USDS holders via an airdrop."

The airdrop is the provision worth noticing. A peg cut alone would simply expropriate stablecoin holders to make the protocol solvent. Pairing it with a fixed 24-billion-SKY distribution converts the haircut into a forced conversion: holders lose dollar value and receive governance-token equity in the recapitalized system instead. It is the debt-for-equity swap of a corporate restructuring, pre-committed in the rulebook rather than negotiated after the fact.

Pre-committing has real effects even if never used. It tells USDS holders in advance what a failure pays them, which bounds the incentive to run: exiting early avoids the haircut but forfeits the airdrop. And because the SKY amount is fixed while the deficit is not, the per-holder compensation dilutes with the severity of the event — the airdrop is a defined quantity of equity, not a make-whole.

Note that the amount is stated absolutely rather than as a share of supply, so what 24 billion SKY represents depends on how much SKY the preceding Backstop Event already minted.
description: If the Prime Agent's capital, Aggregate Backstop Capital and the SKY Backstop are all exhausted, the peg is set below $1 to settle the deficit and USDS holders receive a SKY airdrop.
